title: Convert Trinity Ram and Rewrite to Dsl Derive Engine
description: Convert trinity_ram (trinity/ram/rs/lib.rs) and trinity_rewrite (trinity/rewrite/engine/rs/lib.rs) from their hand-rolled DocumentDsl/OpText parsers onto the dsl:: derive engine, in that order (rewrite depends on ram). Use local structural-twin types for foreign-typed fields (Manifest/TrinityManifest is out of scope for full DSL round-trip since only manifest_id is ever textually round-tripped; PortDirection needs a twin since it is foreign and re-exported for trinity_jack/trinity_plugin/framework consumers we must not break). Do not touch trinity_jack, trinity_plugin, framework/*, or any dsl/* engine crate. Verify with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-trinity-dslconv-target cargo test -p trinity_ram -p trinity_rewrite.
summary:
Converted trinity_ram then trinity_rewrite from hand-rolled vcs::DocumentDsl/OpText parsers onto the dsl:: derive engine, in dependency order.

trinity_ram (trinity/ram/rs/lib.rs): manifest-prep step confirmed to cover ONLY PropertyValue/PropertyBag (a hand-written impl dsl::DslField for PropertyValue via Shape::Value) - Manifest/TrinityManifest/KindDef/PropertyDef/ValueType were NOT touched. Investigated GraphFixture.manifest's actual DSL role: the OLD hand-rolled grammar never round-tripped the full Manifest through text either (only manifestId, resolved via resolve_manifest()/manifest_by_id), so no local-twin tree for Manifest was needed at all - it's simply absent from the new GraphFixtureDsl mirror, reconstructed via resolve_manifest() same as before. Built local twins only for the two fields that ARE genuinely printed as data: PortDirection (foreign, re-exported for trinity_jack/trinity_plugin/framework - kept its real shape untouched, added PortDirectionDsl twin) and EntityRef (local but tuple-variant-of-String, which dsl::DslEnum's newtype codegen cannot bind - kept its real tuple shape untouched for trinity_jack compatibility, added a flat EntityRefDsl{kind,id} twin). Added dsl::DslRecord directly to Camera and Edge (no foreign fields). Built PortDsl/NodeDsl mirrors (Port/Node transitively carry the foreign direction field) and GraphFixtureDsl/TrinityGraphOperationDsl mirrors, with hand-written DocumentDsl+DslField impl for GraphFixture and OpText impl for TrinityGraphOperation delegating to the mirrors. Found TWO external fixture files the task brief said didn't exist: trinity/example/nakagin-capsule-tower.trinity and branch-chain.trinity (loaded via include_str! in tests). Followed the mandatory regen procedure: temporarily reintroduced the old parser's PARSE half (reconstructed from the pre-edit file content) in a throwaway #[test], parsed both fixtures with it, printed with the NEW print_dsl, wrote back, reparsed with the NEW parser, asserted equality - passed, then deleted the temp test+old parse fns together. Removed now-dead old hand-rolled grammar (print_port/parse_port, print_node_line/parse_node_fields, print_edge_line/parse_edge_fields, entity_kind_and_id/parse_entity_and_key, print_property_bag/parse_property_bag, quote_text, and the old DocumentDsl/OpText impls); kept dsl_lex/DslParser/DslTok and print_property_value/parse_property_value_line/parse_property_value_line (still used, still pub, still consumed by trinity_rewrite... actually no longer consumed after its own conversion, but kept since they have their own dedicated passing unit tests and are a reasonable standalone value-literal codec). Updated 2 tests whose assertions checked old-format error-message text to match the new engine's own error strings (still asserting "malformed input is rejected", just via a different message). Result: 67/67 tests pass (real `cargo test -p trinity_ram` run).

trinity_rewrite (trinity/rewrite/engine/rs/lib.rs): confirmed via dsl_core source that plain String fields already round-trip embedded newlines/quotes correctly through the engine's own Shape::Text (escape_text/unescape_text), so before_fixture_json/lhs_json/rhs_json needed zero changes. Changed parameter_bindings from HashMap<String,PropertyValue> to BTreeMap (no call site relied on HashMap ordering - only tests/DSL code touched it). Added a local LayoutPoint{x,y} DslRecord twin for rule_layout's (f64,f64) tuple value (dsl::DslField has no impl for raw tuples) with From<(f64,f64)>/From<LayoutPoint> conversions, changed rule_layout to BTreeMap<String, LayoutPoint>. Since every field is now DSL-ready directly (no foreign types reachable), derived #[derive(dsl::DslDocument)] directly on RewriteRuleState and #[derive(dsl::DslOps)] directly on RewriteRuleOperation - no mirror types needed at all for this crate. RewriteRuleDiff correctly left undecorated (pure internal OperationDiff snapshot type, never round-tripped through DSL text). Deleted the entire old hand-rolled quote_blob/parse_quoted_blob + DocumentDsl/OpText impls. Updated the 2 tests whose assertions/inputs were tied to the old line-based grammar text/error messages (one rewritten to build its fixture via print_dsl/parse_dsl round-trip instead of hardcoded old-format text; two error-message substring assertions updated to match the new engine's messages). Result: 44/44 tests pass (real `cargo test -p trinity_rewrite` run).

Final combined verification: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-trinity-dslconv-target cargo test -p trinity_ram -p trinity_rewrite → trinity_ram 67/67 passed, trinity_rewrite 44/44 passed, 0 failed in both. Did not touch trinity_jack, trinity_plugin, framework/*, or any dsl/* engine crate.
